facts.raw_span: A patient in their 70s presented with dyspnea and fatigue
No history of structural heart disease or hypertension
Medical history significant for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago, treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy
Blood pressure: 96/54 mm Hg
Heart rate: 56 bpm
Serum troponin I: 0.04 ng/mL (normal value, <0.02 ng/mL)
NT-proBNP: 3896.83 pg/mL (normal value, <100 pg/mL)
Present ECG shows prolonged P-wave duration (180 milliseconds), positive-negative biphasic P wave in leads II, III, and aVF, with shortened or disappeared PR segment
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Revealed diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, measuring approximately 50 mm × 22 mm
PET-CT scan: Showed significantly increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium

concepts.why: The patient's history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, as well as increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium, suggest cardiac involvement by lymphoma.
The patient's elevated NT-proBNP, abnormal ECG findings, and increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium suggest pericardial disease.
The patient's elevated NT-proBNP and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium suggest restrictive cardiomyopathy.
The patient's elevated NT-proBNP and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium suggest cardiac amyloidosis.

The patient's history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and the presence of diffuse medium masses in the right atrium, as well as increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium, suggest metastatic disease to the heart.

rationales.F03: History of lymphoma increases the likelihood of cardiac lymphoma.
rationales.F07: Elevated NT-proBNP suggests heart failure, which can be caused by various conditions including cardiac lymphoma and restrictive cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F09: Masses in the right atrium are highly suggestive of cardiac lymphoma or metastatic disease.
rationales.F10: Increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium supports the diagnosis of cardiac lymphoma or metastatic disease.
